newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers steady, W. Africa mln barrels active.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers steady, W. Africa mln barrels active.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates generally held firm on Monday, with a further very large crude carrier fixed from Iraq, brokers said.

The 260,000 tonne D'Artagnan was fixed Iraq/west at W57.5 for Texaco, loading March 26. One broker dismissed reports that the vessel was destined for South Africa, following a BP Iraqi fixture last week bound for Durban.
Brokers said the rate for Mideast/Japan VLCCs remained at about W60 and to Singapore at W57.5.

The 130,000 tonne (million barrel) West Africa/U.S. market was active with the 1994-built African Ruby carrying 134,000 tonnes to USAC fixed at W106.5 for Sun, and the 1976-built, 130,000 tonne Psara fixed at W103.75, also for Sun.

West Africa VLCCs were quieter and little changed at about W70. This sector has picked up recently, averaging W72.42 in the period March 3-6 against W68.06 between Feb 7 and March 6, according to Reuters Tanker Industry Index (punch in RTII9 and Enter).
One broker said the 80,000 tonne cross-Med sector was showing a softer tone on a lack of enquiry, although this was partly due to public holidays in Russia and Greece.

He said cargoes were being fixed at W100-107.5, with much depending on dates and the quality of the vessel. The same applied to 130,000 tonners, which were being fixed at "not less than W100," he added.
Inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonners edged up to W130 from W125 on good enquiry and a lack of tonnage, although brokers said this sector was also date-sensitive.

Med 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes firmed to W225 from about W200 on a lack of prompt vessels and good enquiry from ENEL, while inter-U.K./Cont slipped to W185/190 from W200. "A lot of vessels have moved from the Med to the Continent, so there are too many ships (in the north) and a lack of cargoes," one broker said.
The Caribs/upcoast market was fairly quiet, with 70,000 tonnes stable at W190 and 50,000 tonnes of fuel oil also steady at W205, U.S. brokers said.
